sanskrit: pra somasya pavamānasyormaya indrasya yanti jaṭharaṁ supeśasaḥ | dadhnā yad īm unnītā yaśasā gavāṁ dānāya śūram udamandiṣuḥ sutāḥ ||
english: The streams of Soma Pavamāna, beautifully formed, flow onward into the belly of Indra; when lifted up with curds and the glorious milk of cows, the pressings have exhilarated the hero, making him fit to give gifts.

sanskrit: acchā hi somaḥ kalaśāṁ asiṣyadad atyo na voḻhā raghuvarttanir vṛṣā | athā devānām ubhayasya janmano vidvāṁ aśnoty amuta itaś ca yat ||
english: For Soma streams straight into the vessels, the bull, like a swiftly-running chariot horse of light gait; knowing both classes of the gods' offspring, he attains what lies there and what lies here.

sanskrit: ā naḥ soma pavamānaḥ kirā vasv indo bhava maghavā rādhasō mahaḥ | śikṣā vayodho vasave su cetunā mā no gayam āre asmat parā sicaḥ ||
english: O Soma Pavamāna, pour wealth upon us; O Indu, be bountiful, a lord of great bounty; instruct the life-increasing Vasu with good counsel; spill not our household goods far away from us.

sanskrit: ā naḥ pūṣā pavamānaḥ surātayo mitro gacchantu varuṇaḥ sajoṣasaḥ | bṛhaspatiḥ maruto vāyur aśvinā tvaṣṭā savitā su yamā sarasvatī ||
english: Let Pūṣan, Pavamāna of good gifts, come to us, and Mitra, Varuṇa of one accord; Bṛhaspati, the Maruts, Vāyu, the Aśvins, Tvaṣṭṛ, Savitṛ well-guiding, and Sarasvatī.

sanskrit: ubhe dyāvāpṛthivī viśvaminve aryamā devo aditir vidhātā | bhago nṛśaṁsa urv antarikṣaṁ viśve devāḥ pavamānaṁ juṣanta ||
english: Both Heaven and Earth, all-encompassing, Aryaman the god, Aditi the establisher, Bhaga, Nṛśaṁsa, broad Antarikṣa — may all the gods delight in Soma Pavamāna.

sanskrit: asāvi somo aruṣo vṛṣā harī rājeva dasmo abhi gā acikradat | punāno vāram pary ety avyayaṁ śyeno na yoniṁ ghṛtavantam āsadam ||
english: Soma the ruddy bull has been pressed, with his two tawny steeds; the skilled one has bellowed toward the cows like a king; purifying himself, he passes around the eternal woolen filter and, like a falcon, has settled into his ghee-rich seat.

sanskrit: kavir vedhasyā pary eṣi māhinam atyo na mṛṣṭo abhi vājam arṣasi | apasedhan duritā soma mṛḷaya ghṛtaṁ vasānaḥ pari yāsi nirṇijam ||
english: O sage, you encompass the great ordinance of the wise creator; like a groomed race horse you rush toward the prize; driving away sin, O Soma, be gracious; clothed in ghee, you move around your splendid garment.

sanskrit: parjanyaḥ pitā mahiṣasya parṇino nābhā pṛthivyā giriṣu kṣayaṁ dadhe | svasāra āpo abhi gā utāsaran saṁ grāvabhir nasate vīte adhvare ||
english: Parjanya is the father of the leafy bull; his abode is established on the mountains, at earth's navel; the sister-waters have flowed about the cows; at the desired sacrifice he meets with the pressing stones.

sanskrit: jāyeva patyāv adhi śeva maṁhase pajrāyā garbha śṛṇuhi bravīmi te | antar vāṇīṣu pra carā su jīvase 'nindyo vṛjane soma jāgṛhi ||
english: Like a wife bestowing dear gifts upon her husband, hear me, O embryo of the Pajra clan — I speak to you; move well among the praises for good living; O Soma, blameless, awaken in the assembly.

sanskrit: yathā pūrvebhyaḥ śatasā amṛdhraḥ sahasrasāḥ paryayā vājam indo | evā pavasva suvitāya navyase tava vratam anv āpaḥ sacante ||
english: As you have been unwearying for our forebears, winning hundreds and thousands, go forth to the prize, O Indu; so now flow for our new well-being; the waters follow your ordinance.

sanskrit: pavitraṁ te vitataṁ brahmaṇas pate prabhur gātrāṇi pary eṣi viśvataḥ | atatpatanūr na tad āmo aśnute śṛtāsa id vahantaḥ tat sam āśata ||
english: Your purifying strainer is spread wide, O Lord of Sacred Speech; the mighty one, you pass around all limbs on every side; one whose body is untested does not attain that — only those who are fully prepared, bearing it, come together to that goal.

sanskrit: tapoṣ pavitraṁ vitataṁ divas pade śocanto asya tantavo vy asthiran | avanty asya pavītāram āśavo divaḥ pṛṣṭham adhi tiṣṭhanti cetasā ||
english: The purifying strainer of the glowing one is spread wide at heaven's station; his blazing threads have spread out; the swift ones stand on the back of heaven with understanding, helping his purifier.

sanskrit: arūrucad uṣasaḥ pṛśnir agriya ukṣā bibharti bhuvanāni vājayuḥ | māyāvino mamire asya māyayā nṛcakṣasaḥ pitaro garbham ā dadhuḥ ||
english: The dappled, firstborn one has blazed forth from the Dawns; the bull, eager for prizes, bears the worlds; the wise ones measured him out with his own creative power; the seers, the fathers, have placed the embryo.

sanskrit: gandharva itthā padam asya rakṣati pāti devānāṁ janimāny adbhutaḥ | gṛbhṇāti ripuṁ nidhayā nidhāpatiḥ sukṛttamā madhuno bhakṣam āśata ||
english: The Gandharva guards his station thus and, wondrous, protects the births of the gods; the lord of treasuries seizes the enemy with a snare; the most skilled ones have partaken of the portion of the honey.

sanskrit: havir haviṣmo mahi sadma daivyaṁ nabho vasānaḥ pari yāsy adhvaram | rājā pavitraratho vājaṁ āruhaḥ sahasrabhṛṣṭir jayasi śravo bṛhat ||
english: Rich in oblations, wearing the great divine seat like a garment, you traverse the sacrifice clothed in cloud; O King whose chariot is the strainer, you have mounted the prize; O Soma of a thousand points, you win great glory.

sanskrit: pavasva devamādano vicarṣaṇir apsā indrāya varuṇāya vāyave | kṛdhī no adya varivaḥ svastimad urukṣitau gṛṇīhi daivyaṁ janam ||
english: Flow and purify yourself, O gladdener of gods, far-perceiving, watery one, for Indra, for Varuṇa, for Vāyu; make ample and blessed space for us today; in the broad dwelling, laud the divine folk.

sanskrit: ā yas tasthau bhuvanāny amartyo viśvāni somaḥ pari tāny arṣati | kṛṇvan saṁcṛtaṁ vicṛtam abhiṣṭaya induḥ siṣakty uṣasaṁ na sūryaḥ ||
english: He who, immortal, has stood within the worlds — Soma streams around all of them; making the assembled into separate streams for the conqueror, Indu cleaves to the Dawn as the Sun does.

sanskrit: ā yo gobhiḥ sṛjyata oṣadhīṣv ā devānāṁ sumna iṣayann upāvasuḥ | ā vidyutā pavate dhārayā suta indraṁ somo mādayan daivyaṁ janam ||
english: He who is mingled with the cows, let loose into the plants, sending forth the grace of the gods — the dear guest; Soma, pressed, flows with his stream bright as lightning, gladdening Indra and the divine folk.

sanskrit: eṣa sya somaḥ pavate sahasrajid dhinvāno vācam iṣirām uṣarbudham | induḥ samudram ud iyarti vāyubhir indrasya hārdi kalaśeṣu sīdati ||
english: This Soma flows purifying himself, winning thousands, stimulating the swift speech that awakens at dawn; Indu, stirred up by the wind-forces, raises up the ocean and sits in the vessels at Indra's heart.

sanskrit: abhi tyaṁ gāvaḥ payasā payovṛdhaṁ somaṁ śrīṇanti matibhiḥ svarvidam | dhanañjayaḥ pavate kṛtvyo raso vipraḥ kaviḥ kāvyenā svarcanāḥ ||
english: The cows adorn with milk that Soma who grows strong with milk and wins the heavenly light through prayers; the sap that wins wealth flows, efficacious; the inspired seer, the poet, is adorned with poetic wisdom.

sanskrit: indrāya soma suṣutaḥ pari sravāpāmīvā bhavatu rakṣasā saha | mā te rasasya matsata dvayāvino draviṇasvanta iha santv indavaḥ ||
english: O Soma, well-pressed, flow around for Indra; let disease depart along with the Rakṣas; may the two-faced ones not enjoy your juice; let the drops that bring wealth be here among us.

sanskrit: asmān samarye pavamāna codaya dakṣo devānām asi hi priyo madaḥ | jahi śatrūṁr abhy ā bhandanāyataḥ pibendra somam ava no mṛdho jahi ||
english: O Pavamāna, spur us on in battle; you are the skill of the gods, their beloved exhilaration; smite the enemies who come to provoke; drink the Soma, O Indra, and crush our foes.

sanskrit: adabdha indo pavase madintama ātmendrasya bhavasi dhāsir uttamaḥ | abhi svaranti bahavo manīṣiṇo rājānam asya bhuvanasya niṁsate ||
english: O Indu, most exhilarating, undeceived, you flow and become Indra's own highest abode; many inspired thinkers sing to you in praise and touch the king of this world.

sanskrit: sahasraṇīthaḥ śatadhāro adbhuta indrāyenduḥ pavate kāmyam madhu | jayan kṣetram abhy arṣā jayan apa uruṁ no gātuṁ kṛṇu soma mīḍhvaḥ ||
english: A thousand-pathed, hundred-streamed, wondrous Indu flows for Indra with the desirable honey; winning the field, stream toward it, winning the waters — O generous Soma, make broad space for our path.

sanskrit: kanikradat kalaśe gobhir ajyase vy avyayaṁ samayā vāram arṣasi | marmṛjyamāno atyo na sānasir indrasya soma jaṭhare sam akṣaraḥ ||
english: Roaring loudly, you are anointed with the cows' milk in the vessel; you stream evenly through the eternal woolen strainer; being polished like a victorious horse, O Soma, you flow together into Indra's belly.

sanskrit: svāduḥ pavasva divyāya janmane svādur indrāya suhavītunāmne | svādur mitrāya varuṇāya vāyave bṛhaspataye madhuma ādābhyaḥ ||
english: Flow sweet for the divine birth; flow sweet for Indra of the good invocation name; flow sweet for Mitra, for Varuṇa, for Vāyu; O inviolable one rich in honey, for Bṛhaspati.

sanskrit: atyam mṛjanti kalaśe daśa kṣipaḥ pra viprāṇām matayo vāca īrate | pavamānā abhy arṣanti suṣṭutim indraṁ viśanti madirāsa indavaḥ ||
english: Ten fingers polish the steed in the vessel; the inspired thoughts of the sages send forth their voices; the purifying drops rush toward the fine praise and enter Indra, the intoxicating Indus.

sanskrit: pavamāno abhy arṣā suvīryam urvīṁ gavyūtim mahi śarma saprathaḥ | mākir no asya pariṣūtir īśa indo jayema tvayā dhanaṁ-dhanam ||
english: O Pavamāna, stream forth with heroic power, broad cattle-pasture, great shelter that spreads wide; let no one be master of this pressing against us — O Indu, may we conquer wealth upon wealth with you.

sanskrit: adhi dyām asthād vṛṣabho vicakṣaṇo arūrucad vi divo rocanā kaviḥ | rājā pavitraratho aty eti rorvad divaḥ pīyūṣaṁ duhate nṛcakṣasaḥ ||
english: The far-seeing bull has mounted to the sky; the seer has blazed forth, illuminating heaven's luminous regions; the King whose chariot is the strainer passes onward, roaring; the seers of men milk the nectar of heaven.

sanskrit: divo nāke madhujihvā asaścato venā duhanty ukṣaṇaṁ giriṣṭhām | apsu drapsaṁ vāvṛdhānaṁ samudra ā sindhor ūrmā madhumantam pavitra ā ||
english: Honey-tongued, incessant, on the vault of heaven the loving ones milk the bull dwelling on the mountains; in the waters, the drop waxing strong in the ocean, in the wave of the river — the honey-sweet one in the strainer.

sanskrit: nāke suparṇam upa papti vāṁsaṁ giro venānām akṛpanta pūrvīḥ | śiśuṁ rihanti matayaḥ panipnataṁ hiraṇyayaṁ śakunaṁ kṣāmaṇi sthām ||
english: Unto the fair-winged bird that has flown to the vault of heaven, many songs of the devotees have lamented; the thoughts lick the ever-moving child, the golden bird standing upon the earth.

sanskrit: ūrdhvo gandharvo adhi nāke asthād viśvā rūpā praticakṣāṇo asya | bhānuḥ śukreṇa śociṣā vy adyaut prārūrucad rodasī mātarā śuciḥ ||
english: Erect, the Gandharva has stood upon the vault of heaven, beholding all his forms; the Sun blazed forth with his bright, radiant light; the pure one has shone forth, illuminating both parents, Heaven and Earth.

sanskrit: pra ta āśavaḥ pavamāna dhījavo madā arṣanti raghujā iva tmanā | divyāḥ suparṇā madhumanta indavo madintamāsaḥ pari kośam āsate ||
english: O Pavamāna, your swift, thought-impelled exhilarations stream forth of themselves like light-born drops; the heavenly, fair-winged, honey-sweet Indus, most exhilarating, settle around the vessel.

sanskrit: pra te madāso madirāsa āśavo asṛkṣata rathyāso yathā pṛthak | dhenur na vatsam payasābhi vajriṇam indram indavo madhuvanta ūrmayaḥ ||
english: Your exhilarations, intoxicating and swift, have been sent forth separately like chariot horses; like a cow with milk to her calf, the sweet honey-waves of Indus go toward Indra the wielder of the bolt.

sanskrit: atyo na hiyāno abhi vājam arṣa svarvit kośaṁ divo adrimātaram | vṛṣā pavitre adhi sāno avyaye somaḥ punāna indriyāya dhāyase ||
english: Like a swift horse urged onward, rush toward the prize, the heaven-knowing vessel, the mountain-born child of the sky; the bull Soma, purifying himself on the back of the eternal strainer, flows for Indra's sake.

sanskrit: pra ta āśvīnīḥ pavamāna dhījuvo divyā asṛgran payasā dhārīmaṇi | prāntar ṛṣayaḥ sthāvīrīr asṛkṣata ye tvā mṛjanty ṛṣiṣāṇa vedhasaḥ ||
english: O Pavamāna, your swift, thought-impelled, heavenly streams connected to the Aśvins have been poured forth with milk as their sustaining force; the sages, the ancient ones, have been sent out, who wipe you clean, O seeker of seers, O wise ordainer.

sanskrit: viśvā dhāmāni viśvacakṣa ṛbhvasaḥ prabhos te sataḥ pari yanti ketavaḥ | vyānaśiḥ pavase soma dharmabhiḥ patir viśvasya bhuvanasya rājasi ||
english: O all-seeing one, O skilful one, the rays of you who truly exist, the mighty one, go all around all stations; having pervaded all, you flow, O Soma, by your ordinances; you reign as lord of the entire world.

sanskrit: ubhayataḥ pavamānasya raśmayo dhruvasya sataḥ pari yanti ketavaḥ | yadī pavitre adhi mṛjyate hariḥ sattā ni yonā kalaśeṣu sīdati ||
english: The rays of Pavamāna go on both sides; the beams of the steadfast, true one pass all around; when the tawny one is wiped upon the strainer, he, truly existing, sits down in his proper home, the vessels.

sanskrit: yajñasya ketuḥ pavate svadhvaraḥ somo devānām upa yāti niṣkṛtam | sahasradhāraḥ pari kośam arṣati vṛṣā pavitram aty eti rorvat ||
english: The banner of sacrifice, the author of the good rite, flows and purifies himself; Soma goes to the purifying place of the gods; the bull of a thousand streams rushes around the vessel and passes over the strainer, bellowing.

sanskrit: rājā samudraṁ nadyo vi gāhate apām ūrmiṁ sacate sindhuṣu śritaḥ | adhy asthāt sānu pavamāno avyayaṁ nābhā pṛthivyā dharuṇo maho divaḥ ||
english: The king, the rivers, plunges into the ocean; dwelling in the streams, he follows the wave of the waters; Pavamāna has mounted the eternal back — the sustainer of the great heaven at earth's navel.

sanskrit: divo na sānu stanayann acikradad dyauś ca yasya pṛthivī ca dharmabhiḥ | indrasya sakhyam pavate vivedidat somaḥ punānaḥ kalaśeṣu sīdati ||
english: He has thundered and cried out like the ridge of heaven; Heaven and Earth are his by his own ordinances; recognizing Indra's friendship, Soma flows, purifying himself, and sits in the vessels.

sanskrit: jyotir yajñasya pavate madhu priyam pitā devānāṁ janitā vibhūvasuḥ | dadhāti ratnaṁ svadhāyor apīcyam madintamo matsara indriyō rasaḥ ||
english: The light of sacrifice, the dear honey, flows; the father of the gods, the procreator, rich in manifold wealth, places the hidden treasure in both the self-offering vessels; the most exhilarating, inebriating, potent juice.

sanskrit: abhikrandan kalaśaṁ vājy arṣati patir divaḥ śatadhāro vicakṣaṇaḥ | harir mitrasya sadaneṣu sīdati marmṛjāno avibhiḥ sindhibhir vṛṣā ||
english: Roaring as he rushes toward the vessel, the far-seeing prize-winner and lord of heaven, of a hundred streams; the tawny bull sits in Mitra's abodes, being polished with the sheep-wool and the rivers.

sanskrit: agre sindhūnām pavamāno arṣaty agre vāco agriyo goṣu gacchati | agre vājasya bhajate mahādhanaṁ svāyudhaḥ sotṛbhiḥ pūyate vṛṣā ||
english: Pavamāna flows foremost among the rivers; foremost of speech, he goes first among the cows; he partakes of the great prize, the foremost treasure; the bull, self-armed, is purified by the pressers.

sanskrit: ayam matavāñ chakuno yathā hito avye sasāra pavamāna ūrmiṇā | tava kratvā rodasī antarā kave śucir dhiyā pavate soma indra te ||
english: This one, swift as an inspired bird that is set free, has coursed with his wave through the wool, O Pavamāna; by your own will, O sage, in the space between the two worlds, pure, he flows with insight — O Soma, for you, Indra.

sanskrit: drāpiṁ vasāno yajato divispṛśam antarikṣaprā bhuvanṣv arpitaḥ | svar jajñāno nabhasābhy akramīt pratnam asya pitaram ā vivāsati ||
english: Wearing his mantle, the adorable one that touches heaven, filling the atmosphere, fixed in the worlds; born from the sun, he strides through the sky; he seeks to honor his ancient father.

sanskrit: so asya viśe mahi śarma yacchati yo asya dhāma prathamaṁ vyānaśe | padaṁ yad asya parame vyomany ato viśvā abhi saṁ yāti saṁyataḥ ||
english: He grants great shelter to that person of his who has first attained his station; when his footstep is in the highest heaven, from there he comes together toward all things, well-ordered.

sanskrit: pro ayāsīd indur indrasya niṣkṛtaṁ sakhā sakhyur na pra mināti saṁgiram | marya iva yuvatibhiḥ sam arṣati somaḥ kalaśe śatayāmnā pathā ||
english: Indu has gone forward to Indra's purifying place; like a friend he does not violate his comrade's compact; like a young man he streams together with the young women — Soma in the vessel, by the path of a hundred courses.

sanskrit: pra vo dhiyo mandrayuvo vipanyuvaḥ panasyuvaḥ saṁvasaneṣv akramuḥ | somam manīṣā abhy anūṣata stubho abhi dhenavaḥ payasem aśiśrayuḥ ||
english: Your thoughts, joyful, eloquent, and admirable, have stridden forth in their shared dwelling-places; they have sung to Soma with understanding, with their praises; the milk-cows have caused the milk to flow toward him.

sanskrit: ā naḥ soma saṁyatam pipyuṣīm iṣam indo pavasva pavamāno asridham | yā no dohate trir ahann asascuṣī kṣumad vājavat madhumat suvīryam ||
english: O Soma, O Indu, flow pure as Pavamāna and bring to us the gathered, swollen food that never fails — she who milks for us thrice a day without ceasing: the food rich in grain, rich in prizes, rich in honey, and rich in heroes.

sanskrit: vṛṣā matīnām pavate vicakṣaṇaḥ somo ahnaḥ pratarītoṣaso divaḥ | krāṇā sindhūnāṁ kalaśāṁ avīvaśad indrasya hārdy āviśan manīṣibhiḥ ||
english: The bull, far-seeing, flows among the inspired thoughts; Soma, the extender of days, of dawns, of heaven; active, he has called out to the vessels of the rivers, entering into Indra's heart with the wise seers.

sanskrit: manīṣibhiḥ pavate pūrvyaḥ kavir nṛbhir yataḥ pari kośāṁ acikradat | tritasya nāma janayan madhu kṣarad indrasya vāyoḥ sakhyāya kartave ||
english: The ancient sage flows through the inspired thinkers, has roared around the vessels, yoked by men; bringing forth the name of Trita, he drips with honey — to make the friendship of Indra and Vāyu.

sanskrit: ayam punāna uṣaso vi rocayad ayaṁ sindhubhyo abhavad u lokakṛt | ayaṁ triḥ sapta duduhāna āśiraṁ somo hṛde pavate cāru matsaraḥ ||
english: This one, purifying himself, has lit up the Dawns; this one has become the world-maker for the rivers; this one, having milked out the mixed drink three times seven, the charming, inebriating Soma flows for the heart.

sanskrit: pavasva soma divyeṣu dhāmasu sṛjāna indo kalaśe pavitra ā | sīdann indrasya jaṭhare kanikradan nṛbhir yataḥ sūryam ārohayo divi ||
english: Flow pure, O Soma, in the divine stations; O Indu, being released into the vessel on the strainer; sitting in Indra's belly, roaring, yoked by men — you have caused the sun to rise in the sky.

sanskrit: adribhiḥ sutaḥ pavase pavitra āṁ inda indrasya jaṭhareṣv āviśan | tvaṁ nṛcakṣā abhavo vicakṣaṇa soma gotram aṅgirobhyo avṛṇor apa ||
english: Pressed by the stones, you flow, O Indu, into the strainer, entering into Indra's bellies; you became the far-seeing seer of men, O Soma, and you opened the cow-pen for the Aṅgiras seers.

sanskrit: tvāṁ soma pavamānaṁ svādhyo anu viprāso amadann avasyavaḥ | tvāṁ suparṇa ābharat divas parīndo viśvābhir matibhiḥ pariṣkṛtam ||
english: You, O Soma Pavamāna, the well-thinking inspired singers have exhilarated in succession, seeking your aid; you, O Indu, the fair-winged eagle has brought from beyond heaven, adorned with all hymns.

sanskrit: avye punānam pari vāra ūrmiṇā hariṁ navante abhi sapta dhenavaḥ | apām upasthe adhy āyavaḥ kavim ṛtasya yonā mahiṣā aheṣata ||
english: Being purified in the woolen strainer with its wave, the seven milk-cows sing and flow toward the tawny one; above the lap of the waters, the inspired men lowed to the sage, the great bull in Ṛta's womb.

sanskrit: induḥ punāno ati gāhate mṛdho viśvāni kṛṇvan supathāni yajyave | gāḥ kṛṇvāno nirṇijaṁ haryataḥ kavir atyo na krīḻan pari vāram arṣati ||
english: Indu, purifying himself, plunges through hostilities, making all paths good for the worshipper; the desirable sage, making his garment of cows, plays like a swift horse and streams around the strainer.

sanskrit: asascataḥ śatadhārā abhiśriyo hariṁ navante ava tā udanyuvaḥ | kṣipo mṛjanti pari gobhir āvṛtaṁ tṛtīye pṛṣṭhe adhi rocane divaḥ ||
english: Ceaseless, hundred-streamed, glorious — those wave-like waters chant to the tawny one and flow down; the ten fingers polish him, wrapped round with the cows' milk, upon the third ridge, at heaven's shining region.

sanskrit: tavemāḥ prajā divyasya retaś tvaṁ viśvasya bhuvanasya rājasi | athedaṁ viśvam pavamāna te vaśe tvam indo prathamod dhāmadhā asi ||
english: These creatures are your offspring from the divine seed; you reign over the entire world; so now all this universe, O Pavamāna, is in your will; you, O Indu, are the first, the setter of foundations.

sanskrit: tvaṁ samudro asi viśvavit kave tavemāḥ pañca pradiśo vidharmaṇi | tvaṁ dyāṁ ca pṛthivīṁ cāti jabhriṣe tava jyotīṁṣi pavamāna sūryaḥ ||
english: You are the ocean, O all-knowing sage; these five regions are yours in your ordinance; you have overpowered both heaven and earth; O Pavamāna, the lights, the Sun, are yours.

sanskrit: tvam pavitre rajaso vidharmaṇi devebhyaḥ soma pavamāna pūyase | tvām uśijaḥ prathamā agṛbhṇata tubhyemā viśvā bhuvanāni yemire ||
english: O Soma Pavamāna, you are purified in the strainer for the gods, by the ordinance of the world-space; the Uśij seers first grasped you; for your sake all these worlds have been ordered.

sanskrit: pra rebha ety ati vāram avyayaṁ vṛṣā vaneṣv ava cakradat dhariḥ | saṁ dhītayo vāvaśānā anūṣata śiśuṁ rihanti matayaḥ panipnatam ||
english: The chanter comes forward, passing through the eternal strainer; the tawny bull has bellowed downward in the forests; the devotional thoughts, lowing in longing, have sung in harmony; the inspired thoughts lick the ever-moving child.

sanskrit: sa sūryasya raśmibhiḥ pari vyata tantuṁ tanvānas trivṛtaṁ yathā vide | nayan ṛtasya praśiṣo navīyasīḥ patir janīnāṁ upa yāti niṣkṛtam ||
english: He, wrapped round by the rays of the sun, weaves his thread as if making a triple braid; leading the newest commandments of Ṛta, the lord of women goes to the place of purification.

sanskrit: rājā sindhūnām pavate patir diva ṛtasya yāti pathibhiḥ kanikradat | sahasradhāraḥ pari ṣicyate hariḥ punāno vācaṁ janayann upāvasuḥ ||
english: The king of the rivers, the lord of heaven, flows and purifies himself, going on the paths of Ṛta, roaring; the tawny one of a thousand streams is poured around; purifying himself, bringing forth speech, he is the dear guest.

sanskrit: pavamāna mahy arṇo vi dhāvasi sūro na citro avyayāni pavyayā | gabhastiPūto nṛbhir adribhiḥ suto mahe vājāya dhanyāya dhanvasi ||
english: O Pavamāna, you run through the great flood, brilliant as the sun, through the eternal ones, with your purifying wheel; purified by the hands, pressed by men with stones, you speed for the great prize, for abundant wealth.

sanskrit: iṣam ūrjaṁ pavamānābhy arṣasi śyeno na vaṁsu kalaśeṣu sīdasi | indrāya madvā madyo madaḥ suto divaḥ viṣṭambha upamo vicakṣaṇaḥ ||
english: O Pavamāna, you stream toward refreshment and sustenance; like a falcon you sit in the vessels upon the summit; the pressed-out exhilaration, the inebriating joy, is for Indra — you are the foremost pillar of heaven, the far-seeing one.

sanskrit: sapta svasāro abhi mātaraḥ śiśuṁ navaṁ jajñānaṁ jenyaṁ vipaścitam | apāṁ gandharvam divyaṁ nṛcakṣasaṁ somaṁ viśvasya bhuvanasya rājase ||
english: The seven sister-mothers flow toward the newborn child, the praiseworthy, wise one; the Gandharva of the waters, heavenly, the seer of men — Soma, to reign over the entire world.

sanskrit: īśāna imā bhuvanāni vīyase yujāna indo haritaḥ suparṇyaḥ | tāḥ te kṣarantu madhumat ghṛtaṁ payas tava vrate soma tiṣṭhantu kṛṣṭayaḥ ||
english: Ruling over these worlds, you move with power; O Indu, yoking the tawny, fair-winged mares; may they pour for you their honey-sweet, ghee-rich milk; may the peoples stand in your ordinance, O Soma.

sanskrit: tvaṁ nṛcakṣā asi soma viśvataḥ pavamāna vṛṣabha tā vi dhāvasi | sa naḥ pavasva vasumad dhiraṇyavad vayaṁ syāma bhuvaneṣu jīvase ||
english: You are the seer of men from all sides, O Soma Pavamāna, O bull; you run through all those things; so flow for us bringing wealth and gold — may we live long in the worlds.

sanskrit: govit pavasva vasuvid dhiraṇyavid retodhā indo bhuvanṣv arpitaḥ | tvaṁ suvīro asi soma viśvavit taṁ tvā viprā upa girema āsate ||
english: Flow, finder of cows, finder of wealth, finder of gold, sower of seed, O Indu, fixed in the worlds; you are heroic, O Soma, knower of all — to you, the inspired seers approach and sit to sing.

sanskrit: un madhva ūrmir vananā atiṣṭhipad apo vasāno mahiṣo vi gāhate | rājā pavitraratho vājaṁ āruhat sahasrabhṛṣṭir jayati śravo bṛhat ||
english: The honey wave has stood upright, eager to please; clothed in the waters, the great bull plunges in; the King whose chariot is the strainer has mounted the prize; Soma of a thousand prongs wins great glory.

sanskrit: sa bhandanā ud iyarti prajāvatīr viśvāyur viśvāḥ subharā ahardivi | brahma prajāvad rayim aśvapastyam pīta indu indram asmabhyaṁ yācatāt ||
english: He stirs up blessings, those rich in progeny, all life-giving, all well-nourishing day by day; O Indu, when drunk, may you ask Indra to grant us sacred prayer with offspring, riches, and a household of horses.

sanskrit: so agre ahnāṁ harir haryato madaḥ pra cetasā cetayate anu dyubhiḥ | dvā janā yātayann antar īyate narā ca śaṁsaṁ daivyaṁ ca dhartari ||
english: He, the tawny, desirable exhilaration, first among the days, makes himself known with his mind day by day; moving between two peoples, he goes along — both that of men and the divine ordainer.

sanskrit: añjate vy añjate sam añjate kratuṁ rihanti madhunābhy añjate | sindhor ucchvāse patayantam ukṣaṇaṁ hiraṇyapāvāḥ paśum āsu gṛbhṇate ||
english: They anoint him, they anoint him separately, they anoint him together; they lick his will with honey, they anoint him; in the swelling of the river, the golden-purifying ones seize the flying bull among the waters.

sanskrit: vipaścite pavamānāya gāyata mahī na dhārāty andho arṣati | ahir na jūrṇām ati sarpati tvacam atyo na krīḻann asarad vṛṣā hariḥ ||
english: Sing to the wise Pavamāna; his mighty stream flows, the plant-extract rushes; like a serpent creeping over a parched skin, the tawny bull has rushed along playing like a swift horse.

sanskrit: agrego rājāpyas taviṣyate vimāno ahnāṁ bhuvanṣv arpitaḥ | harir ghṛtasnu sudṛśīko arṇavo jyotīrathaḥ pavate rāya okyaḥ ||
english: The foremost of herds, a royal one, he gains strength; measuring the days, fixed in the worlds; tawny, dripping with ghee, beautifully seen like a flood, he of the light-chariot flows — welcome to the house of wealth.

sanskrit: asarji skambho diva udyato madaḥ pari tridhātur bhuvanāny arṣati | aṁśuṁ rihanti matayaḥ panipnataṁ girā yadi nirṇijaṁ ṛgmiṇo yayuḥ ||
english: The pillar has been loosed, the exhilaration lifted to heaven; the three-natured one streams around the worlds; the inspired thoughts lick the ever-moving stalk — when the singers have gone with song to his shining garment.

sanskrit: pra te dhārā aty aṇvāni meṣyaḥ punānasya saṁyato yanti raṁhayaḥ | yad gobhir indo camvoḥ samajyasa ā suvānaḥ soma kalaśeṣu sīdasi ||
english: Your streams, O ram, passing over the finest things of the purifying one, the gathered ones, run swiftly; when, O Indu, you are mingled with the cows in the bowls, O pressed Soma, you sit in the vessels.

sanskrit: pavasva soma kratuvīn na ukthyo avyo vāre pari dhāva madhu priyam | jahi viśvān rakṣasa indo atriṇo bṛhad vadema vidathe suvīrāḥ ||
english: Flow pure, O Soma, our praise-worthy one possessed of resolve; run around the dear honey in the woolen strainer; O Indu, smite all the Rakṣas, all the devourers; may we, endowed with good heroes, speak great words at the ceremony.

sanskrit: pra tu drava pari kośaṁ ni ṣīda nṛbhiḥ punāno abhi vājam arṣa | aśvaṁ na tvā vājinam marjayanto acchā barhi raśanābhir nayanti ||
english: Now run forward, sit down around the vessel; purified by men, stream toward the prize; polishing you like a prize horse, they lead you toward the sacrificial grass with their reins.

sanskrit: svāyudhaḥ pavate deva indur aśastihā vṛjanaṁ rakṣamāṇaḥ | pitā devānāṁ janitā sudakṣo viṣṭambho divo dharuṇaḥ pṛthivyāḥ ||
english: Self-armed, the divine Indu flows and purifies himself, destroying slander, protecting the enclosure; the father of the gods, the procreator of excellent skill, the pillar of heaven, the support of earth.

sanskrit: ṛṣir vipraḥ purāetā janānām ṛbhur dhīra uśanā kāvyena | sa cid viveda nihitaṁ yad āsām apīcyaṁ guhyaṁ nāma gonām ||
english: He is the inspired seer, the forerunner of peoples, the skillful and wise one, Uśanas by poetic wisdom; he found out what was hidden among them, the secret, concealed name of the cows.

sanskrit: eṣa sya te madhumāṁ indra somo vṛṣā vṛṣṇe pari pavitre akṣāḥ | sahasrasāḥ śatasā bhūridāvā śaśvattamam barhir ā vājy asthāt ||
english: O Indra, this your honey-rich Soma, the bull, has flowed through the strainer for you, the mighty one; winning thousands, winning hundreds, giving abundantly — the prize-winner has ever stood at the sacrificial grass.

sanskrit: ete somā abhi gavyā sahasrā mahe vājāyāmṛtāya śravāṁsi | pavitrābhiḥ pavamānā asṛgrañ chravasyavo na pṛtanājo atyāḥ ||
english: These Soma juices with their thousands of cows stream for great prizes, for immortality, for glories; the purifying ones have been loosed through their purifiers — eager for fame like swift horses born for battle.

sanskrit: pari hi ṣmā puruhūto janānāṁ viśvāsarad bhojanā pūyamānaḥ | athā bhara śyenabhṛta prayāṁsi raviṁ tuñjāno abhi vājam arṣa ||
english: For the much-invoked one goes among peoples, flowing in all directions with his nourishments while being purified; then bring forth your gifts, O you carried by the eagle — spurring on wealth, rush toward the prize.

sanskrit: eṣa suvānaḥ pari somaḥ pavitre sargo na sṛṣṭo adadhāvad arvā | tigme śiśāno mahiṣo na śṛṅge gā gavyann abhi śūro na satvā ||
english: This pressed Soma has run around the strainer, rushing forward like a released torrent; sharpening himself like a great bull with his horns, he rushes toward the cows, seeking them like a hero, like a fighter.

sanskrit: eṣā yayau paramād antar adreḥ kūcit satīr ūrve gā viveda | divo na vidyut stanayanty abhraiḥ somasya te pavata indra dhārā ||
english: He came from the furthest interior of the rock; hidden though they were, he found the cows in the broad place; thundering with the clouds like lightning from the sky, O Indra, this stream of your Soma flows.

sanskrit: uta sma rāśim pari yāsi gonām indreṇa soma saratham punānaḥ | pūrvīr iṣo bṛhatīr jīradāno śikṣā śacīvas tava tā upaṣṭut ||
english: And you circle the herd of cows, O Soma, purifying yourself on the same chariot with Indra; O swift giver, bestow upon us many great refreshments and food supplies; O powerful one, strengthen those praises of yours.

sanskrit: ayaṁ soma indra tubhyaṁ sunve tubhyam pavate tvam asya pāhi | tvaṁ ha yaṁ cakṛṣe tvaṁ vavṛṣa indum madāya yujyāya somam ||
english: This Soma, O Indra, is pressed for you, it flows purified for you — drink of it; you have fashioned him and chosen Indu, the Soma, for exhilaration and youthful strength.

sanskrit: sa īṁ ratho na bhuriṣāḻ ayoji mahaḥ purūṇi sātaye vasūni | ād īṁ viśvā nahuṣyāṇi jātā svarṣātā vana ūrdhvā navanta ||
english: Like a well-yoked chariot of great wealth, he has been harnessed for the winning of many and great riches; then all things born of Nahuṣa's race, the sky-winning ones, have cried upward in the forest.

sanskrit: vāyur na yo niyutvāṁ iṣṭayāmā nāsatyeva hava ā śambhaviṣṭhaḥ | viśvavāro draviṇodā iva tman pūṣeva dhījavan o si soma ||
english: Like Vāyu who has his team, well-impelled on his journey, most beneficent in answer to prayer like the Nāsatyas — you are all-desired, bestowing wealth by yourself like Draviṇodas, O Soma, swift of thought like Pūṣan.

sanskrit: indro na yo mahā karmāṇi cakrir hantā vṛtrāṇām asi soma pūrbhit | paidvo na hi tvam ahināmnāṁ hantā viśvasyāsi soma dasyoḥ ||
english: Like Indra who has performed great deeds, you are the slayer of Vṛtras, O Soma, the breaker of strongholds; for you, like Paidva, are the slayer of the serpent-brood; O Soma, you are the slayer of every Dasyu.

sanskrit: agnir na yo vana ā sṛjyamāno vṛthā pājāṁsi kṛṇute nadīṣu | jano na yudhvā mahata upabdir iyarti somaḥ pavamāna ūrmim ||
english: Like Agni when released in the forest, freely bestowing splendours in the rivers; like a warrior against a great one, with his roaring, Soma Pavamāna stirs up his wave.

sanskrit: ete somā ati vārāṇy avyā divyā na kośāso abhravarṣāḥ ||
english: These Soma juices have passed through the woolen strainer, like heavenly vessels pouring rain from the cloud.

sanskrit: śuṣmī śardho na mārutam pavasv ānabhiśastā divyā yathā viṭ | āpo na makṣū sumatir bhavā naḥ sahasrāpsāḥ pṛtanāṣān na yajñaḥ ||
english: Flow mightily like a troop of Maruts, O strong one; uncondemned, like the heavenly clan; be quick well-thinking toward us, like the waters — O Soma of a thousand forms, like a sacrifice that conquers armies.

sanskrit: rājño nu te varuṇasya vratāni bṛhad gabhīraṁ tava soma dhāma | śuciṣ ṭvam asi priyo na mitro dakṣāyyo aryamevāsi soma ||
english: Your ordinances are truly those of King Varuṇa; great and deep is your station, O Soma; you are pure, dear like Mitra, powerful in skill like Aryaman, O Soma.

sanskrit: pro sya vahniḥ pathyābhir asyān divo na vṛṣṭiḥ pavamāno akṣāḥ | sahasradhāro asadann y asme mātur upasthe vana ā ca somaḥ ||
english: Onward the carrier shoots along the paths; Soma Pavamāna, like rain from the sky, has streamed; the thousand-streamed one has settled in us — Soma both in the mother's lap and in the forest.

sanskrit: rājā sindhūnām avasiṣṭa vāsa ṛtasya nāvam āruhadrajiṣṭhām | apsu drapsaḥ vāvṛdhe śyenajūto duha īm pitā duha īm pitur jām ||
english: The king of the rivers has put on his garment; he has mounted the straightest ship of Ṛta; the drop, swift as a falcon, has waxed mighty in the waters; the father milks it, and milks the daughter of his father.

sanskrit: siṁhaṁ nasanta madhvo ayāsaṁ harim aruṣaṁ divo asya patim | śūro yutsu pratamaḥ pṛcchate gā asya cakṣasā pari pāty ukṣā ||
english: They acclaim as a lion the inexhaustible one of the honey, the tawny, ruddy lord of this sky; the hero, foremost in battle, he seeks the cows; the bull watches over with his eye.

sanskrit: madhupṛṣṭhaṁ ghoram ayāsam aśvaṁ rathe yuñjanty urucakra ṛṣvam | svasāra īṁ jāmayo marjayanti sanābhayo vājinam ūrjayanti ||
english: The honey-backed, terrible, inexhaustible horse they yoke to the chariot, the wide-wheeled and exalted one; the sisters, the kinswomen, wipe him clean; those of the same navel strengthen the prize-winner.

sanskrit: catasra īṁ ghṛtaduhaḥ sacante samāne antar dharuṇe niṣattāḥ | tā īm arṣanti namasā punānās tā īṁ viśvataḥ pari ṣanti pūrvīḥ ||
english: Four ghee-milking ones accompany him, seated within the same supporting place; they stream toward him with reverence as he purifies himself; the many ancient ones surround him from all sides.

sanskrit: viṣṭambho divo dharuṇaḥ pṛthivyā viśvā uta kṣitayo haste asya | asat ta utso gṛṇate niyutvān madhvo aṁśuḥ pavata indriyāya ||
english: He is the pillar of heaven, the support of earth; all peoples are in his hand; may that source be his for the singers — the stalk of honey, accompanied by his team, flows for Indra's power.

sanskrit: vanvann avāto abhi devavītim indrāya soma vṛtrahā pavasva | śagdhi mahaḥ puruścandrasya rāyaḥ suvīryasya patayaḥ syāma ||
english: Winning, unchecked, toward the divine feast, flow, O Soma Vṛtrahān, for Indra; grant us great wealth rich in many splendours — may we be lords of heroic power.

sanskrit: pra hinvāno janitā rodasyo ratho na vājaṁ saniṣyann ayāsīt | indraṁ gacchann āyudhā saṁśiśāno viśvā vasu hastāyor ādadhānaḥ ||
english: Impelling himself forward, the begetter of Heaven and Earth has gone forth like a chariot about to win the prize; going to Indra, sharpening his weapons, placing all good things in his two hands.

sanskrit: abhi tripṛṣṭhaṁ vṛṣaṇaṁ vayodhām āṅgūṣāṇām avāvaśanta vāṇīḥ | vanā vasāno varuṇo na sindhūn vi ratanaddhā dayate vāryāṇi ||
english: The voices of the singers have lowed toward the three-ridged, virile, life-sustaining one; like Varuṇa clothed in the forests, like the rivers, the treasure-placer distributes the desirable things.

sanskrit: śūragrāmaḥ sarvavīraḥ sahāvāñ jetā pavasva sanitā dhanāni | tigmāyudhaḥ kṣipradhānvā samatsv aṣāḷhaḥ sāhvān pṛtanāṣu śatrūn ||
english: O hero among heroes, possessing all heroes, mighty in strength, a conqueror — flow and win wealth; sharp-weaponed, swift-bowed, unconquered in combats, having overpowered the enemies in battles.

sanskrit: urugavyūtir abhayāni kṛṇvan samīcīne ā pavasv āpuraṁdhī | apaḥ siṣāsann uṣasaḥ svar gāḥ saṁ ciikrado maho asmabhyaṁ vājān ||
english: O you of wide cattle-pasture, making safety on both sides, flow into the full intelligence; seeking to win the waters, the Dawns, the sunlight, the cows — roar together for us the great prizes.

sanskrit: matsi soma varuṇam matsi mitram matsīndram indo pavamāna viṣṇum | matsi śardho mārutam matsi devān matsi mahām indram indo madāya ||
english: O Soma, gladden Varuṇa, gladden Mitra; O Indu Pavamāna, gladden Indra, gladden Viṣṇu; gladden the troop of Maruts, gladden the gods; O Indu, gladden great Indra for exhilaration.

sanskrit: evā rājeva kratumāṁ amena viśvā ghanighnad duritā pavasva | indo sūktāya vacas vayo dhā yūyam pāta svastibhiḥ sadā naḥ ||
english: Thus flow, purposeful and vigorous like a king, destroying all evils; O Indu, give sustenance to the well-spoken word — do you ever protect us with blessings.
